newsitem.title: USA: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - bid wanted lists clip prices.
newsitem.headline: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - bid wanted lists clip prices.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices recovered from session lows to end down 3/8 to 1/4 of a point as Treasuries pared losses, but talk of much as $500 million of bid-wanted lists being circulated still weighed on prices.
Most of the sellers who posted their bonds for sale were looking to get rid of intermediate issues, traders said, but added that opinions appeared to have split over the market's near-term direction.
Potential buyers included those who seemed to be looking for prices to firm, as they sought issues with lower coupons, which would climb faster in a rally.
"Five-percent came into vogue because of their convexity and duration," a trader said, but noted that some issues with higher yields, like 5-1/2 percent, were seen as less desirable.
Other types of bonds that were sought-after included those with longer call protection, traders said.
And some players remained cautious, noting that the municipal market is nearing levels last seen in March. "Everytime you get a new high, you want to become a little more cautious," a trader said.

While soothed by the Federal Open Market Committee's decision to leave interest rates unchanged at Wednesday's meeting in Washington, the market remained on edge about the release on Thursday at 0830 EDT of the Consumer Price Index.
A 0.3 percent rise for October was predicted by a Reuters consensus survey of economists.

December futures on the Chicago Board of Trade ended at 116-27/32, down 10 ticks. And the December Treasury bond futures closed at 114-23/32, off six ticks. This left the MOB spread at 68 ticks, unchanged from levels seen around midday.

This week's and next week's new issues calenders are fairly light, especially when measured against some of the huge volumes sold last month, and new issues were considered fairly aggressively priced by some players.
"Some seem a little full, yes," a trader said, but noted that several competitive deals appeared to have been specifically tailored for certain institutional buyers, making them easier to place.

Philadelphia sold $58.9 million of lease bonds, which were priced at a 5.75 percent top yield in 2027, while Boston sold $90 million of general obligation bonds at a true interest cost of 4.94 percent.

In the secondary market, actively traded issues included Cook County Illinois Refunding Capital Improvement of November 2022, which have a 5-7/8 percent coupon. The bonds were bid at 100-1/2, unchanged.
And Metropolitan Pier & Exposition Authority Illinois Dedicated State Tax Revenue Refunding of June 2027, which pay a 5-1/4 percent coupon, were bid at 5.71 percent NET, up four basis points.
